name: GO Classes CS 2025 | Weekly Quiz 27 | Normalization, Relational Model | Question

question.text:
Following table has two attributes Employee_id and Manager_id, where Employee_id is a primary key and manager_id is a foreign key referencing Employee_id with on-delete cascade:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \text{Employee_id} & \text{Manager_id} \\ \hline 20 & 40 \\ \hline 25 & 40 \\ \hline 30 & 35 \\ \hline 35 & 20 \\ \hline 40 & 45 \\ \hline 45 & 25 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

On deleting the table $(20,40)$, the set of other tuples that must be deleted to maintain the referential integrity of table is

  1. $(30, 35)$ only
  2. $(30, 35)$ and $(35, 20)$ only
  3. $(35, 20)$ only
  4. $(40, 45)$ and $(25, 40)$ only

Consider the following functional dependencies in a database:

  • $A \rightarrow B$
  • $B \rightarrow C$
  • $D \rightarrow E$
  • $E \rightarrow D$
  • $F \rightarrow G$
  • $F \rightarrow H$
  • $(E,F) \rightarrow I$

The relation $(E,D,A,B)$ is

  1. $2$ NF
  2. $3$ NF
  3. BCNF
  4. None of the above

Consider a Relation $\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{ABCD})$. For which of the following set of functional dependencies (FDs), relation $\mathrm{R}$ is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)?

  1. $\mathrm{BD} \rightarrow \mathrm{AC} ; \mathrm{AB} \rightarrow \mathrm{D} ; \mathrm{AC} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$
  2. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{C} ; \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{AC} ; \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{D}$.
  3. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{BCD} ; \mathrm{B} \rightarrow \mathrm{ACD}$
  4. $\mathrm{BC} \rightarrow \mathrm{AD} ; \mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$

Consider the following relational schema and set of functional dependencies.

$\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{E})$ with functional dependencies $\mathrm{ABC} \rightarrow \mathrm{D} ; \mathrm{CD} \rightarrow \mathrm{A} ; \mathrm{AD} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}$.

Which of the following is true?

  1. $R$ is in $1 \mathrm{NF}$ but not in $2 \mathrm{NF}$.
  2. $R$ is in $2 \mathrm{NF}$ but not in $3 \mathrm{NF}$.
  3. $\mathrm{R}$ is in $3 \mathrm{NF}$ but not in BCNF.
  4. $\mathrm{R}$ is in BCNF.

Consider the following relation state for $R(A, B, C)$

Which of the following dependencies may hold in the above relation?

  1. $A B \rightarrow C$
  2. $C \rightarrow A B$
  3. $B \rightarrow C$
  4. $A C \rightarrow B$

Consider the functional dependencies (FDs) of a relation $\mathrm{R}$ and below-mentioned properties:

  • $\text{P1:}$ A non-prime attribute determines a different non-prime attribute.
  • $\text{P2:}$ A proper subset of a candidate key determines a non-prime attribute.

Choose the correct option:

  1. If some FD of $\mathrm{R}$ has property $\mathrm{P} 1, \mathrm{R}$ can't be in $2 \mathrm{NF}$
  2. If some FD of $\mathrm{R}$ has property $\mathrm{P} 2, \mathrm{R}$ can't be in $2 \mathrm{NF}$
  3. $\mathrm{P} 1$ and $\mathrm{P} 2$ won't affect $\mathrm{R}$ being in $2 \mathrm{NF}$
  4. If some FD of $\mathrm{R}$ has property $\mathrm{P} 2, \mathrm{R}$ can still be in $2 \mathrm{NF}$

An attribute $A$ is called prime if $A$ is in any of the candidate keys. Assume in the following statements, $\mathrm{A}$ is an attribute $\&\;\mathcal{X}$ is a set of attributes.

Consider the following statements:

  1. Domain of each attribute is an elementary type; that is, not a set or a record structure.
     
  2. Whenever $\mathcal{X} \mapsto A$ is a functional dependency that holds in relation $\mathbf{R}$ and $A \notin \mathcal{X}$, then either
    • $A$ is prime, or
    • $\quad \mathcal{X}$ is a key or a super-key for $\mathbf{R}$.
       
  3. Whenever $\mathcal{X} \mapsto A$ is a functional dependency that holds in relation $\mathbf{R}$ and $A \notin \mathcal{X}$, then either
    • $A$ is prime, or
    • $\mathcal{X}$ is not a proper subset of any key for $\mathbf{R}$.
       
  4. Whenever $\mathcal{X} \mapsto A$ is a functional dependency that holds in relation $\mathbf{R}$ and $A \notin \mathcal{X}$, then
    • $\mathcal{X}$ is a key or a super-key for $\mathbf{R}$.

Which of the following is a correct match??

  1. $\text{A – 1NF, B – 2NF, C – 3NF, D – BCNF}$
  2. $\text{A – 1NF, B – BCNF, C – 2NF, D – 3NF}$
  3. $\text{A – 1NF, B – 3NF, C – 2NF, D – BCNF}$
  4. $\text{A – BCNF, B – 3NF, C – 2NF, D – 1NF}$

Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. Each superkey is a superset of some candidate key.
  2. Each primary key is also a candidate key, but there may be candidate keys that are not primary keys.
  1. only $1$ is true
  2. only $2$ is true
  3. both $1$ and $2$ are true
  4. neither $1$ nor $2$ are true

Which of the following statements best describes the main reason for representing a relational database in BCNF?
  1. To achieve physical data independence.
  2. To remove data anomalies (insertion, update, deletion anomalies).
  3. To save space on disk.
  4. To achieve logical data independence.

Consider the relation $\mathbf{R}(\underline{\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}}, \mathbf{C}, \mathbf{D}, \mathbf{E}, \mathbf{F})$ with $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$ as a composite primary key and the following dependencies:

  • $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{E}, \mathrm{F}$
  • $\mathrm{E} \rightarrow \mathrm{D}$
  • $\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{F}$

Which of the following options are true? (Select all correct choices)

  1. $\mathrm{R}$ is in $3 \mathrm{NF}$ (i.e. $3^{\text {rd }}$ Normal Form)
  2. $\mathrm{R}$ is in $2 \mathrm{NF}$ (i.e. $2^{\text {nd }}$ Normal Form)
  3. $\mathrm{R}$ is in $1 \mathrm{NF}$ (i.e. $1^{\text {st }}$ Normal Form)
  4. $\mathrm{R}$ is in $2 \mathrm{NF}$ but not in $3 \mathrm{NF}$

Suppose $R$ and $S$ are two relations. Let $C$ be the referential integrity constraint that says: whenever $R$ has a tuple with some values $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_n$ in particular attributes $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$, there must be a tuple of $S$ that has the same values $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_n$ in particular attributes $B_1, B_2, \ldots, B_n$.

Which of the following operations on $R, S$ can cause violation of the constraint $\mathrm{C}?$

  1. Insert into $\mathrm{R}$
  2. Insert into $\mathrm{S}$
  3. Delete from $\mathrm{R}$
  4. Delete from $\mathrm{S}$

Consider the relational schema $\text{R(A B C D)}$ with following functional dependency set $F=\{A\rightarrow BC,C\rightarrow D\};$ The relation $\text{R}$ is in

  1. $2$ NF
  2. BCNF
  3. $3$ NF
  4. $1$ NF

Consider the following relational schema and set of functional dependencies.

$R(A, B, C, D, E)$ with functional dependencies $A B \rightarrow E$ and $D \rightarrow C$. Let $\mathrm{X}$ be the number of superkeys for this relation.

Let $Y$ be the number of minimal superkeys for this relation. What is $\mathrm{X}+\mathrm{Y}?$

Consider the relational scheme $\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}, \mathrm{E}, \mathrm{F}, \mathrm{G}, \mathrm{H})$ and the following functional dependencies over $$\mathrm{R} : \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{BCD} ; \mathrm{AD} \rightarrow \mathrm{E} ; \mathrm{EFG} \rightarrow \mathrm{H} ; \mathrm{F} \rightarrow \mathrm{GH}$$

Based on these functional dependencies, there is one key for $\mathrm{R}$. One of these four functional dependencies can be removed without altering the key. Which one?

  1. $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{BCD}$
  2. $\mathrm{AD} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}$
  3. $\mathrm{EFG} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}$
  4. $\mathrm{F} \rightarrow \mathrm{GH}$

Which one of the following statements about normal forms is $\text{FALSE}?$
  1. $\text{BCNF}$ is stricter than $\text{3NF}$
  2. Lossless, dependency-preserving decomposition into $\text{3NF}$ is always possible
  3. Lossless, dependency-preserving decomposition into $\text{BCNF}$ is always possible
  4. Any relation with two attributes is in $\text{BCNF}$
